pharm: Topical antibiotic active against Gram-positive bacteria, including Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes
quick: Apply a small amount to affected area 3 times daily for 10 days
Use only if clearly needed; systemic absorption negligible
Caution; avoid application to the nipple if breastfeeding
Avoid large-area/prolonged use due to PEG vehicle (ointment) in severe impairment
Clinical response; re-evaluate if no improvement in 3-5 days
summary: Mupirocin is a topical antibacterial that inhibits bacterial isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase, used to treat secondarily infected traumatic skin lesions caused by susceptible Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes. It is for topical use only and not for intranasal, ophthalmic or mucosal use (cream formulation).
indications: Treatment of secondarily infected traumatic skin lesions (up to 10 cm in length or 100 cm2 in area) due to susceptible Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes (cream)
Topical treatment of impetigo (ointment, where labelled)

dosage.d: Apply a small amount to the affected area 3 times daily
dosage.n: Re-evaluate if no response in 3-5 days

dosage.d: Apply a small amount 3 times daily (per labelled age)

admin: Apply with a cotton swab or gauze pad; cover with gauze if desired
Not for intranasal, ophthalmic or other mucosal use (cream)
Do not apply concurrently with other lotions, creams or ointments
Re-evaluate if no clinical response within 3-5 days
moa: Mupirocin reversibly and specifically binds bacterial isoleucyl-transfer-RNA synthetase, halting incorporation of isoleucine into bacterial proteins and thereby inhibiting protein and RNA synthesis. Its unique mechanism means no cross-resistance with other antibiotic classes.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to mupirocin or any component
relative: Application over large open wounds (PEG vehicle absorption in renal impairment for ointment)

preg: There are no adequate well-controlled studies in pregnant women; systemic absorption after topical use is negligible. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether mupirocin is excreted in human milk after topical use. Use with caution; if applied to the chest, wash the area before breastfeeding and avoid the nipple.
renal: Negligible systemic absorption with cream. The polyethylene glycol vehicle in the ointment can be absorbed from large/open wounds; avoid such use in moderate-to-severe renal impairment.

minor: Do not co-apply other topical products at the same site (may reduce efficacy)

common: Burning, stinging or pain at application site
rare: Superinfection with non-susceptible organisms including fungi

monitoring: Local reactions and signs of sensitisation
Possible overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms with prolonged use
counsel: Apply only to the affected skin three times a day for the full course
Wash hands before and after application
Do not use in the eyes, nose or mouth (cream)
Do not apply other creams/ointments at the same site
Return if the infection does not improve within 3-5 days
pk: Any absorbed drug rapidly metabolised to inactive monic acid
Store at 20-25 C; do not freeze
pearls: Unique mechanism - no cross-resistance with other antibiotic classes
Topical only; cream not for intranasal/mucosal use (nasal ointment is a distinct product)
Limit to 10 days to reduce resistance
Avoid large-area ointment use in renal impairment (PEG vehicle)
missed: Apply the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next application, skip it and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.
overdose: Topical overdose is unlikely to cause systemic effects given negligible absorption. Ingestion is not expected to be toxic in small amounts; manage supportively.
